reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be the full finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel space with its canonical full-space volume, including dimension zero and all approved ambient instances. Let W:E->R be C1 and assume exp(-W) is integrable against volume. Define mu=volume.tilted(x->-W(x)), the actual normalized Gibbs measure exp(-W)/integral exp(-W) times volume. In this full-space setting the approved context gives the positive normalized density; no separate positive-partition hypothesis is a displayed binder in this statement.
For every real-linear partial operator D:L2(mu;R)->L2(mu;E), assume D is closable and its graph is characterized exactly as follows: for every scalar L2 class a and vector L2 class H, (a,H) belongs to D.graph iff there exists a smooth compactly supported real function phi:E->R with a=phi mu-almost everywhere and H=gradient(phi) mu-almost everywhere. D.closure is the genuine single-valued operator from that same graph closure, with its actual submodule domain.
Then for every u in this SAME D.closure.domain, if D.closure(u)=0 as an actual vector L2(mu) class, there exists a real c with (u as a scalar L2(mu) representative)(x)=c for mu-almost every x.
D is fixed before every u. The constant c is selected after u and may depend on u; no universal common constant for all zero-output elements is claimed. The premise is equality of the true closed-gradient output to the zero vector quotient, not a claim that the rough representative's totalized derivative vanishes pointwise. C1 regularity of W suffices here and no curvature, positive spectral gap, dense-domain condition or mean-zero assumption is added. This is a universal implication for a supplied closable exact-gradient D, not an existential construction of D. It is one direction only: zero output implies weighted-AE constancy. It does not produce constant-function domain membership or prove full kernel equality, nor a centered/epsilon-zero/range/Poincare or further inequality/core/composition theorem. There is no joint measurable choice of constants.
objects: C1 real potential W,actual normalized Gibbs measure mu; original supplied real-linear scalar-to-vector weighted L2 partial gradient D with exact smooth compact graph and genuine closure; arbitrary closure-domain u with zero vector L2 output; existential real c for its weighted-AE representative.
domains: Full finite real Hilbert/Borel E,canonical volume,including0. W:E->R; mu=volume.tilted(-W). D between actual scalar Lp R 2 mu and vector Lp E 2 mu,on a submodule domain. u belongs to D.closure.domain,closure output equality to0 in genuine vector L2; standard representative constancy mu-AE. Input exp(-W) integrability uses volume.
quantifiers: Universal E,W subject to C1 and exp(-W) integrability; let mu; forall D,closable and exact graph iff antecedents (forall scalar a/vector H,exists smooth compact phi) -> forall u:SAME D.closure.domain,D.closure u=0 -> exists c:R,scalar representative equals constant mu-AE. c is after u; D fixed before every u.
assumptions: W C1; actual volume Integrable exp(-W); D.IsClosable; D.graph exactly smooth compact real function/gradient pairs modulo mu; u closure-domain and actual vector output=0. No separately displayed hZ positivity binder,curvature,spectral gap,dense-domain assumption,mean-zero condition or rough classical fderiv hypothesis.
conclusion: For every zero-output u of this same closed-gradient operator,exists real c such that its actual scalar quotient representative is c mu-AE.
scopes: One-way zero-gradient implication only,not production of constants in domain or full kernel equality. Universal D implication is not a D existence theorem. Constants may differ across u. Full-space context and real C1 W retained; no resolvent/epsilon/f/cutoff quantifiers or quantitative inequalities appear here. No joint measurable selection or additional centered/range/core/main/composition assertion.
constant_dependencies: Existential c may depend on W,mu,D,u; no common c for all u,no estimate constant or curvature parameter. Quotient exponent2,zero output actual vector quotient0; normalized density exp(-W)/partition exactly.
